Fucking why. What the fuck would additional "gun control" accomplish? He was already a fucking convicted felon! He should have never had a goddamn gun to begin with! We have people trying to enact laws to regulate something they know nothing about! How is this even possible?!

There is a "gun control" issue I could see myself supporting. Public access to NICS. It would have to operate completely differently from the way it currently does, but it can be done.

It wouldn't be a seller-driven process. It would be buyer-driven. The buyer would conduct the check from the comfort of his own web browser, and he'd receive a confirmation code from NICS to provide to the seller. The code would be valid for 30 days. The seller would anonymously verify the code through the same website.

Conducting a check (or anonymously verifying a check) is no longer directly linked to a purchase, so there is less risk of the government building a viable gun registry. They might know that you conducted a check, but they have no idea if you bought a gun at all, let alone how many guns you might have purchased in that 30 day period.

Providing this tool would likely mitigate one of the issues I see in the law. We are currently prohibited from selling to felons, but the way the courts are interpreting the law, we are prohibited from knowingly selling to felons. If a felon poses as a buyer but doesn't disclose that he's a felon, he can (theoretically) acquire a gun without the seller having committed a crime. The courts have determined that because there is no reasonable way for the seller to know this information, it would be a miscarriage of justice to prosecute the seller in this situation, and criminal liability lies with the felon. Unfortunately, this gives an incentive (or the appearance of an incentive) for the seller to remain willfully ignorant of the buyer's status. It entices sellers to behave irresponsibly.

But, the moment we provide reasonable access to NICS, the courts can reverse themselves. They can read the prohibition against selling to felons as a duty to verify the buyer's status. If done this way, then the fact that a buyer could have passed a background check at the time of transfer becomes prima facie evidence that the seller has fulfilled that duty. You can't be charged for trading guns with your shooting buddies; but the irresponsible "sellers" among us can more readily be charged for providing guns to prohibited buyers.

Ultimately, this "gun control" issue would expand the private market. We'd have more people willing to trade guns privately because they have the tools to do it responsibly. If the courts react as I expect they would, it would also accomplish every one of the few reasonable goals of UBCs, but without the bullshit hassles that UBCs entail. Because it accomplishes all the same goals, it destroys the push to enact UBCs.

I think we should stop waiting around, having gun control advocates constantly asking for concessions. I think we should go out and demand public access to NICS. Bloomberg, Watts, et al would likely come out against this plan because it destroys their hassle-rich UBC plans, demonstrating that they're not concerned in the slightest about public safety, but only about hassling responsible gun owners.
